title: Building Maintenance Specialist
description: Black Hills State University invites qualified, self-motivated candidates for a Building Maintenance Specialist for the Facilities Services Department. DUTIES: This position will be expected to maintain the heating and cooling systems of the campus and keep them in proper working order. Perform preventive, predictive, and scheduled maintenance and repairs to the HVAC and Boiler systems. RESPONSIBILITIES: Work on all campus HVAC equipment: Boilers & boiler controls Water heaters Basic energy monitoring on central and remote systems Coordinate the above HVAC work with all other facets of maintenance SUCCESSFUL CANDIDATES WILL HAVE: Experience with managing workflow processes and balancing multiple tasks simultaneously. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy. Ability to make decisions independently and to determine when consultation with supervisor is required. Ability to establish and maintain professional relationships with students, faculty, staff and the public. QUALIFICATIONS: Required: Minimum of three years of HVAC work in the field or three full years of school or a combination of both. Acquire a license within 6 months of employment. Must have working knowledge of computers, knowledge of local and national mechanical and building codes, basic knowledge of electrical controls, several years of experience in boiler controls, be able to lift heavy loads, be able to climb ladders, stairs, and scaffold, be able to work long and late hours should the need arise. COMMENTS: Periodically will be required to work at the Rapid City Campus. Typical office hours are Monday through Friday 7:00AM-3:30PM. After hours ON CALL will be required on a rotation basis. Sponsorship not available for this position. TO APPLY: Applications must be made online at https://yourfuture.sdbor.edu . Candidates will need to attach a cover letter, resume and the names/contact information of at least three professional references. This position is open until filled with a first review date of September 28, 2026 at 11PM mountain time. For application assistance, please contact Human Resources at 605.642.6549. Questions specific to the position may directed towards Scott Hansen at 605.642.6244 or at Scott.Hansen@bhsu.edu. Arrangements for accommodations required by disabilities can be made by contacting Cassie Maser at 605-642-6545 or Cassie.Maser@bhsu.edu . title: Help Desk Analyst
description: Black Hills State University seeks applicants for a Help Desk Analyst in our Network and Computer Services department. This position serves as a key customer-facing member of the Information Technology team and requires exceptional customer service, communication, and problem-solving skills. RESPONSIBILITIES: - Manage university Help Desk operations and ensure faculty, staff, students, and other customers receive timely, professional, and courteous technical support; - Interview, select, train, schedule, supervise, and evaluate Help Desk student employees; - Develop, maintain, and revise Help Desk protocols, procedures, technical documentation, knowledge-based articles, and service standards; - Administer and support assigned systems, including TeamDynamix and the Druva endpoint backup system; - Coordinate TeamDynamix administration, standards, and processes with other South Dakota Board of Regents administrators; - Configure and deploy computers for faculty and staff and support state-owned computers, applications, printers, scanners, and peripheral devices; - Apply and maintain operating system patches, hotfixes, updates, and upgrades; - Create, test, maintain, and deploy standardized computer images; - Diagnose and resolve hardware, software, account-access, connectivity, and network-related problems; - Manage file permissions and security for network shares; - Plan, test, document, and implement system upgrades and related procedures; - Accurately document, categorize, prioritize, track, and escalate service requests; - Provide end-user support by telephone, email, live chat, remote-support tools, and in person; and - Maintain positive, professional relationships and communicate clearly with university customers and technology staff. KNOWLEDGE OF: - Microsoft Windows operating systems; - Microsoft 365 applications; - macOS operating systems and applications; - Networking concepts, protocols, connectivity, and troubleshooting; - Computer design, installation, configuration, compatibility, and operating system principles; - Information security concepts, practices, and principles; - A diverse range of computer hardware, software, and peripheral devices. ABILITY TO: - Explain technology and information security issues clearly to nontechnical individuals; - Communicate clearly, concisely, and professionally with students, parents, faculty, staff, administrators, and other stakeholders; - Provide courteous and effective customer service to individuals with varying levels of technical knowledge; - Supervise, train, mentor, and support Help Desk student technicians; - Assist with planning and implementing campus-wide technology projects; - Diagnose and resolve technical problems independently; - Collaborate effectively with BHSU technology and support staff; - Develop and implement system-wide technology solutions; - Anticipate potential issues and take appropriate preventive action; - Collect, evaluate, and analyze technical information from multiple sources and system components; - Maintain current technical knowledge of hardware, software, security, and industry developments; - Research, evaluate, and implement innovative technologies; - Lift and move computer equipment weighing up to 50 pounds. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: - A bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience is preferred. CERTIFICATIONS: - The Lenovo Certified Warranty Technician exam will need to be completed in the first three months of employment. REQUIRED LICENSE: - A valid driver’s license is required. COMMENTS: This is a full-time, 12-month, overtime-eligible position. Normal working hours are 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. Travel is required. The position is performed primarily in office and classroom environments and includes supervising and directing Help Desk student technicians.  Sponsorship is not available for this position. TO APPLY: Applications for this position must be made online at http://yourfuture.sdbor.edu. Complete the online application and attach a cover letter, resume, and the names and contact information for three professional references. This position is open until filled with a first review date of September 7, 2026 @ 11PM Mountain Time. For application assistance, please contact Human Resources at 605.642.6549. title: Financial Aid Advisor
description: Black Hills State University is seeking a dynamic, student-focused professional to join our Student Financial Aid Office as a Financial Aid Advisor. This position is an integral part of the Enrollment Management team and is based on the Spearfish campus. The Financial Aid Advisor serves as a key resource for students and families navigating the financial aid process. This position provides personalized financial aid counseling, supports the administration of federal and institutional aid programs, and helps students understand their options for financing their education. The ideal candidate is approachable, organized, detail-oriented, and committed to helping students succeed. Financial aid can be complex, and we are looking for someone who can turn complicated regulations and processes into information students and families can understand and use. This position is grant funded for two years, with the intention of transitioning to a university-funded position following the grant period. Key Responsibilities: • Provide comprehensive, individualized financial aid counseling to prospective and current students and their families regarding federal, state, institutional, and alternative financial aid programs. • Explain financial aid eligibility, award requirements, policies, deadlines, and student responsibilities in a clear and student-friendly manner. • Respond to student and family inquiries by phone, email, and in person with professionalism, accuracy, and a commitment to excellent customer service. • Review and process financial aid information and documentation in accordance with federal, state, and university regulations. • Manage Satisfactory Academic Progress (SAP) processes, including monitoring, student communication, and review of SAP appeals. • Coordinate and administer the Federal Work-Study (FWS) program, including awarding, monitoring, tracking, and communication with students and campus departments. • Utilize the National Student Loan Data System (NSLDS) and other federal and institutional systems to research student eligibility and financial aid history. • Maintain accurate student records and ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, and university policies and regulations. • Collaborate with campus partners across Enrollment Management and other university departments to support student enrollment and retention. • Participate in financial aid outreach activities, including financial aid workshops, FAFSA information nights, student orientations, and other recruitment or enrollment events. • Stay current on changes to federal and state financial aid regulations, institutional policies, and financial aid programs. • Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned. Minimum Qualifications: • Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience. • 1–3 years of general office or administrative experience. • Strong written and verbal communication skills. • Strong interpersonal and customer service skills with the ability to work effectively with students, families, faculty, staff, and campus partners. • Ability to explain complex information clearly to individuals with varying levels of knowledge and experience. • Ability to exercise sound judgment, maintain confidentiality, and handle sensitive student information appropriately. • Ability to work independently while also contributing effectively as part of a collaborative team. • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. Preferred Qualifications: • Previous experience working in financial aid or higher education. • Experience with Banner Student Information System (SIS) or another student information system. • Knowledge of federal financial aid regulations, including FAFSA, Federal Pell Grant, Direct Loans, Federal Work-Study, and Satisfactory Academic Progress. • Experience counseling students or providing financial aid advising. • Experience working with NSLDS or other federal financial aid systems. Comments: Sponsorship is not available for this position. To Apply: Applications must be made online at https://yourfuture.sdbor.edu . Candidates will need to attach a cover letter, resume and the names/contact information of at least three professional references. This position is open until filled with a first review date August 31, 2026 at 11pm mountain time. For application assistance, please contact Human Resources at 605.642.6549. Questions specific to the position may directed towards Tirzah Knight at Tirzah.Knight @bhsu.edu . Arrangements for accommodations required by disabilities can be made by contacting Cassie Maser at 605-642-6545 or Cassie.Maser@bhsu.edu . Employment is dependent upon a satisfactory background check.

title: Assistant Professor, Biology (Organismal Zoology)
description: The School of Natural Sciences at Black Hills State University invites applicants for a full-time, tenure-track, Assistant Professor position in organismal zoology, beginning August 2026. The successful candidate will join a diverse Natural Science department and complement other faculty in areas of ecology, evolution, physiology, genetics and cell-molecular biology. DUTIES: The successful candidate will help shape and grow the new wildlife emphasis within the Biology major by teaching upper-level courses that support wildlife students (ecology, mammalogy, herpetology, ichthyology, environmental policy, etc), as well as introductory courses in Biology as needed. We seek a broadly trained wildlife biologist or ecologist who will complement existing faculty strengths in the School of Natural Sciences and develop collaborations with local and regional agencies. Individuals with expertise in wildlife or fisheries management are especially encouraged to apply. Primary responsibilities include successful teaching and advising, development of a research program that includes undergraduate and graduate students, and service related to student professional opportunities. Other opportunities include supervision of graduate students in the Integrative Genomics MSc. program, and course instruction in the Sustainability MSc. program. QUALIFICATIONS: A PhD in Biology, Wildlife Ecology, Natural Resources or related field. ABD accepted. COMMENTS: The School of Natural Sciences at Black Hills State University is a vibrant, growing division with approximately 23 faculty members in biology, chemistry, geology, and physics. Faculty emphasize undergraduate teaching and mentoring, and conduct research involving students in multiple biological and environmental disciplines. Projects are funded through a variety of state wildlife, federal agency, and partnership grants. Research resources include the largest Herbarium in the state, and well-equipped laboratories including a scanning electron microscopy lab. The Center for the Conservation of Biological Resources (CCBR) is a shared research laboratory containing research space and commonly used equipment required for genetics and genomics research. WestCore is a Genetics/Genomics sequencing core facility that provides services including NextGen genome, transcriptome, and Sanger sequencing, genotyping, and quantitative real-time PCR services. WestCore also houses a cell culture area and an RNA isolation room. The Black Hills State University Underground Campus (BHUC) at the Sanford Underground Research Facility (SURF) in Lead, SD houses Sanford Lab’s low background counting facility, a class-1,000 cleanroom, and an adjoining workspace available for use in a variety of disciplines. Managed by BHSU, the underground campus partners with groups around the globe to create unique opportunities for collaborative research in physics, chemistry, biology, and geophysics. SPECIAL COMMENTS: The successful applicant must be authorized to work in the United States. Sponsorship is not available for this position. TO APPLY: Applications must be made online at http://yourfuture.sdbor.edu. Please submit a cover letter, curriculum vitae, a statement of teaching philosophy, statement of proposed research, transcripts, and names and contact information for at least three professional references. Letters of reference/recommendation are not accepted. (Please note, you may need to combine documents into one file to upload into the system.) This position is open until filled with a first review date of June 19, 2026 at 11:00 PM (mountain time). For application assistance, contact Human Resources at 605.642.6549. Please direct inquiries regarding the position to Dr. Jessica Graham, search committee chair, at Jessica.Graham@bhsu.edu. Arrangements for accommodations required by disabilities can be made by contacting Cassie Maser at 605-642-6545 or Cassie.Maser@bhsu.edu.
